item.title: Australia and Turkey criticised for hosting UN climate conference while embracing coal
item.description:
Global campaign group 350.org urges Cop31 hosts to announce a coal phase-out date and national roadmaps to get off fossil fuels

  • Sign up for climate and environment editor Adam Morton’s free Clear Air newsletter here

The hosts of the next major United Nations climate conference, Turkey and Australia, are facing criticism for being partners in a coal supply chain while remaining near silent on the need for a global deal to rapidly get off fossil fuels.

With the Cop31 summit in the Turkish Mediterranean city of Antalya just a month away, the two countries running the fortnight-long talks have been accused by activists of a “vacuum of action” on plans for a transition away from coal, gas and oil – a key goal of many nations at the talks.

item.title: Yemen’s Saudi-backed government launches military drive to retake all Houthi-held territory
item.description:
The announcement came hours after Iranian-backed Houthis reportedly cut a vital supply route to besieged city of Taiz

Yemen’s Saudi-backed government has announced the start of a new military operation to retake all territory held by the Houthis, even as the militant group made fresh gains on the ground, reportedly encircling a government-held city.

Rashad al-Alimi, the head of Yemen’s presidential council, said in a statement on Sunday: “I announce today the start of military operations to retake the remaining territories of the republic and extend the authority of the state and its institutions across the entire national territory.”

item.title: Suicide by plane or terrorism? Speculation over motive in flight 1073 attack
item.description:
Experts sceptical flydubai co-pilot’s only motivation was to end his own life and say key question is means of radicalisation

At about 9.30 on Wednesday morning local time, Tali Manes was taking her six-year-old daughter, Nina, to the toilet on the regular flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv when she heard a series of heavy blows against the cockpit door.

Manes, an Israeli bank executive, immediately told a flight attendant seated nearby that something was wrong. When he did not react, she shouted at him: “Something is happening in there!” Seconds later, the man “simply went to the [cockpit] door and opened it”, Manes told Israel’s Channel 12 TV.

item.title: Strikes by North Sea oil workers could ‘severely disrupt’ UK fuel supplies
item.description:
Union says staff left with no choice but industrial action after breakdown in pay talks with Texas oil firm Apache

A looming strike by oil workers in the North Sea could “severely disrupt” UK fuel supplies, the Unite union has said, adding that staff were left with no choice after a breakdown in pay talks with the Texas oil company Apache.

The union said Apache workers had “emphatically” backed strike action after being given what it said was an unacceptable pay offer that amounted to a real-terms pay cut for many employees, at a time when the company was “raking in eye-watering profits”.

item.title: Explosions reported near tanker off southern Yemen: UKMTO
item.description:
Explosions reported near tanker off southern Yemen: UKMTO

A tanker reported seeing several explosions nearby about 60 nautical miles south of the Yemeni port city of Mocha in the Gulf of Aden on Sunday, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) agency said.

The agency added that the tanker's crew was safe and there was no environmental damage reported.

item.title: Iranian oil minister steps down
item.description:
Iranian oil minister steps down

Iran's oil minister Mohsen Paknejad has resigned, the president's office said in a statement on Sunday, amid long queues at petrol stations caused by the ongoing war and US sanctions.

Government spokesperson Mehdi Tabatabaei told state TV later on Sunday that Paknejad, a member of President Pezeshkian's cabinet since August 2024, resigned for personal reasons "a long time ago."

Hamid Bord, the CEO of the National Iranian Oil Company (NIOC), "has been appointed as acting Minister of Oil by a decree from the president", according to a statement carried by Iran’s state media.

Bord has held senior positions at NIOC and previously headed several of its operating units, including the National Iranian South Oil Company and the Iranian Offshore Oil Company.

item.title: Over 70 dead in fighting around Yemen's Taiz in 24 hours
item.description:
Over 70 dead in fighting around Yemen's Taiz in 24 hours

More than 70 people have been killed over the past day in fighting in and around the southwestern Yemeni province of Taiz, AFP reported on Sunday, citing sources from both sides.

Sources from the Yemeni government reported that 34 troops were killed, 20 of them in neighbouring Lahj, on the edge of Taiz province.

Houthi military sources said 39 of their fighters were killed in fighting across Taiz and in areas bordering Lahj.

The Yemeni government announced earlier on Sunday that it had launched a new wave of military operations to reclaim Houthi-controlled territory.

The same day, the Houthis cut a vital supply route linking Taiz with Aden, the interim capital of the internationally recognised government.

item.title: Mecca pact committee to meet in Riyadh on Monday, Turkey says
item.description:
Mecca pact committee to meet in Riyadh on Monday, Turkey says

A committee of the Mecca defence pact between Turkey, Saudi Arabia, and Pakistan will hold talks in Riyadh on Monday, the Turkish foreign ministry said on Sunday.

"The meeting will address recent developments in the region and the stage reached in the Alliance’s institutionalisation efforts," the Turkish statement said.

Pakistan's foreign minister said on Friday that Iran had suggested engaging Yemen's Houthis politically after attacks by the group, an idea that the Mecca defence pact committee would discuss at a meeting in Riyadh this week.
